title: Geometric constant-module comparison data
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be sites small relative to a coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], with independent object and morphism universes, and $A$ a commutative ring. Use the constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], their ringed module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and actual normalized constant-scalar restrictions [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]. GeometricData consists of a geometric adjunction on set sheaves, its finite-limit-preserving inverse image with its algebraic ring and module lifts, a constant-section-preserving isomorphism of its inverse-image constant ring with the target constant ring, scalar-extension module pullback, its specified generalized pure-tensor comparison and module adjunction with underlying direct-image Hom normalization, and the induced fixed-scalar adjunction [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-geometric-adjunctions]. It includes the corresponding ringed-topos datum [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with exactly these underlying functors, adjunction, ring map and module direct image. ExactData records additivity, exactness and preservation of the coproducts used in totals of the two pullbacks. OrdinaryIdentification consists of the inverse-image and direct-image isomorphisms under scalar restriction, the underlying direct-image identity and their full Hom equation. FixedTensorData consists of the underlying inverse-image comparison, its Hom normalization, a strong monoidal structure and the generalized pure-tensor equation. With ordinary uncompleted derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], DerivedTensorIdentification consists of monoidal structures on ringed ordinary pullback and both localized pullbacks, the given ordinary ringed tensor comparison, the two K-flat total normalization squares [def-sfb-derived-projection-comparison-squares]. These are definitions of packages and predicates, with no existence assertion. The ringed-topos datum is the landed independent-universe ringed-topos morphism [def-pur-ringed-topos-morphism-of-universes], at the coefficient universe of the sites. The independent-universe fixed-scalar adjunction interface in this module retains the generalized-element module equations of the cited notion. Its constant-scalar comparison helper states the same normalized direct-image, inverse-image, Hom, unit, counit and further-left-adjoint conclusions for these interfaces, without changing either cited node's Lean record.

proof.text: The structures and predicates are the displayed packages, with no existence assertion. For the constant_scalar_geometric_adjunctions_ofUniverses helper, construct the scalar map out of the sheafified terminal presheaf. The terminal presheaf is already a sheaf; naturality of its sheafification unit and the constant/forgetful comparison identify every scalar section with the constant-ring sheafification unit. This calculation works with independent object and morphism universes.

Compose the supplied underlying direct-image isomorphisms to obtain theta. Apply the module_linear equation of RingedToposMorphismOfUniverses and the fixed-scalar linear equation to b*x+y. The constant-section normalization identifies the scalar inputs, and injectivity of the sheaf adjunction gives preservation of this operation. Evaluate at the projections of the product sheaf to obtain sectionwise linearity; derive additivity and zero preservation. Bundle the resulting linear natural maps and use reflection of isomorphisms by the module forgetful functor to construct beta with its required underlying equation.

Use the existing adjunctionSquare theorem from ConstantScalarGeometricAdjunctions, now exported with its original statement and proof. It constructs the invertible mate of beta across fully faithful horizontal functors with essentially surjective target, and supplies the normalized Hom, unit and counit equations. The generic helper already has independent category universes; no second copy or universe adaptation is needed.

The existing constant-ring restriction equivalences supply full faithfulness and essential surjectivity at both sites. Apply adjunctionSquare to the supplied ringed and fixed-scalar adjunctions with beta to obtain alpha and its three equations. Apply it again to the supplied further left adjoints, with the sites reversed and right-adjoint comparison alpha, to obtain kappa and its Hom, unit and counit equations. No witness of mere existence is used to define data, and no assumption on points or the coefficient ring is added.
